title: Midweek benchmark heatmap triage notes (Aug 26 2025)
body:
Attendees: Sofia A., Liam O., Priya R., Elias S., Marta L. (quick drop-ins from SRE and infra)

TL;DR
- Midweek heatmap run surfaced two cluster-level regressions: 95th latency uplift on small-seq (64) requests and throughput drop for quantized 8-bit xformers variant at batch sizes > 8.
- Likely correlated with last kernel selection roll (2025-08-20) + new batching heuristic change merged in PR #1298.
- Primary repro steps and trace ids listed below. Action items assigned; short-term rollback option prepared.

What we ran
- Heatmap scope: 6 models (rwkv-7b, meta-7b, redwood-base-3b, redwood-chat-7b), seq lens: [32, 64, 128, 256], batch sizes: [1,4,8,16], quant variants: fp16, int8, q4_0.
- Test harness: bench-runner v2.3.1 (anchored to commit 0a9f3), docker image: redwood/bench:2025-08-24.
- Environment: GCP n2-standard control-plane, GPUs: A10G for most runs, some stress runs on H100 staging.
- Run window: 2025-08-25 22:00 UTC -> 2025-08-26 04:00 UTC.

Key observations
- Small-seq tail latency: 95th percentile increased from 48ms -> ~92ms for seq=64, model=redwood-base-3b, batch=4, int8. 99th also elevated. CPU usage on host spiked concurrently.
- Quant int8 variant throughput regression: int8 xformers variant showed 18-22% lower tokens/sec at batch>=8 vs baseline (fp16) on A10G. Effect smaller on H100.
- KV-cache hit-rate: steady (no change) across runs, so not a cache invalidation issue.
- Batching behavior: we observed increased number of small micro-batches (1-2) at peak request bursts; batching heuristic logs show earlier flush threshold decreased (new heuristic).
- Kernel selection log: recent commit changed default GEMM kernel preference for certain dims. The selection favored kernel C over B starting at commit 2025-08-20.

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) Kernel preference change picked a kernel with worse small-seq latency characteristics on A10G (likely true given the timing).
2) New batching heuristic reduces coalescing, producing more micro-batches and higher CPU scheduling overhead under burst; exacerbates tail latency.
3) int8 path on xformers interacts poorly with the chosen kernel, reducing vectorization efficiency (explains throughput drop).
4) Unrelated infra noise (OOM GC on control-plane) unlikely — control-plane logs clean during run except for short CPU jitter window.

Repro steps (short)
- Quick repro command (bench-runner): bench-runner --model redwood-base-3b --seq 64 --batch 4 --variant int8 --clients 16 --duration 300 --collector heatmap-aug26
- To reproduce on staging with explicit kernel override: bench-runner ... --kernel-preference B (see bench README).
- Relevant trace ids: trace-20250826-1a7, trace-20250826-1b3, trace-20250826-22f (stored in gs://redwood-perf/traces/2025-08-26).
- Logs: /logs/serving-runtime/bench/heatmap-2025-08-26/*.log

Data highlights (numbers)
- redwood-base-3b, seq=64, batch=4, int8: p50 30ms -> 34ms, p95 48ms -> 92ms, p99 120ms -> 280ms.
- meta-7b, seq=128, batch=8, fp16: throughput stable +-3%.
- rwkv-7b showed no measurable regression (different kernel path).

Immediate mitigations considered
- Rollback kernel-preference commit on canary fleet (risk: subtle perf impact elsewhere). Pre-baked rollback PR prepared jenkins/rollback-kernel-pref-aug26.
- Revert/adjust batching heuristic to previous flush threshold for bursty routes; run microbenchmark.
- Force kernel B for int8 xformers variants as temporary workaround.

Action items
- Sofia: run focused microbench on A10G comparing kernel B vs C across seq lengths (due 2025-08-27).
- Priya: prepare canary rollout plan for batching heuristic revert (JIRA-RT-4188) and coordinate with SRE windows (due 2025-08-28).
- Liam: instrument additional batching telemetry (emit micro-batch size distribution metric) and add alert if avg micro-batch<2 under high qps (due 2025-08-29).
- Elias: evaluate int8 xformers perf on H100 to quantify hardware variance; feed data into Optimize recommendations (due 2025-08-29).
- Marta: post mortem skeleton and heatmap visual attached to Confluence page and link PRs (due 2025-09-02).

Open questions / unknowns
- Why did p50 remain modest while p95/p99 ballooned? (Suspect scheduling jitter + micro-batch multiplication).
- Are there customer routes exposed to this pattern (small seq + int8) in prod? Need customer usage query.
- Does kernel B produce regression elsewhere (long-seq or other models)? Need broader regression matrix.

Notes from quick SRE check
- No OOM, no disk pressure. Short CPU steal spike noted on 2025-08-25 23:12 UTC for nodes in zone-3; correlates with worst tail. SRE recommends isolating test nodes from noisy neighbor instance types in next run.

Next sync
- Daily standup update until mitigation completed. Next focused heatmap after kernel tests: target 2025-08-28 02:00 UTC.
- We will decide on rollback vs targeted workaround after Sofia and Elias numbers come in.

Appendix (quick commands and pointers)
- bench-runner repo: github.com/redwood-inference/bench-runner (commit 0a9f3)
- Trace explorer: internal.perf/trace/explorer?trace=trace-20250826-1a7
- Logs (GCS): gs://redwood-perf/traces/2025-08-26/

Notes-to-self: keep samples of the worst traces (store in /tmp/sofia/heatmap-samples) and attach to JIRA-RT-4123.
